case_title: Narender Singh & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 read with ss.148 and 149 (convicted); charged also under ss.147, 149 and 294
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (two injured/eye witnesses), medical evidence, documentary contemporaneous records (FIR, crime details form, applications), recovery of weapons, Section 27 statements, post-mortem evidence
confession: Section 27 statements (Exhibits P18 to P21) were referred to as part of the incriminating evidence; not separately analysed as a confession
aggravating_circumstances: Attack with sharp weapons with intention to kill, by a group; deceased had multiple injuries (8 injuries, four grievous)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 read with ss.148 and 149 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 666 of 2000) dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed by Division Bench, judgment dated 07.09.2006
offence_finally_established: Murder of the Sarpanch under IPC s.302 read with ss.148 and 149
neutral_facts: On the night of 27 June 1997, around 10:00 pm, the victim was sitting and talking with two men, one of them an injured eyewitness, behind a hotel in a village where street lights and a burning chimney gave light. A group of men arrived. One carried a sword, one a farsa, one an axe, and the others lathis. The man with the sword, while abusing the victim and saying he could not escape that day, struck the victim on the head. A farsa blow and an axe blow also landed on the head, and the victim fell. The others struck with lathis. The eyewitnesses and others pleaded for the victim, and the group left after a warning. The injured eyewitness went to a police station about one kilometre away, where a first information report was registered at 10:45 pm. The investigating officer reached the scene between 11:00 and 11:15 pm, inspected it at 11:10 pm, and prepared a crime details form and requests for medical examination of the injured witness and for a post-mortem. A doctor examined the injured witness on the night of the incident and recorded his injuries. The post-mortem found eight injuries on the body, four of them grievous. The body was taken to hospital by 7:30 am on the next day. The accused were arrested on 28 June 1997 and weapons were seized on 29 June 1997 following section 27 statements. The express report reached the magistrate only on 30 June 1997.
physical_harm: Death of the Sarpanch (deceased) from head and other injuries; 8 injuries on body, four grievous. Eyewitness P.W.3 also sustained injuries.
number_of_offences: 5 charged (ss.147, 148, 149, 302, 294 IPC); 1 finally upheld (s.302 read with ss.148 and 149)
motive: alleged: old enmity (as recorded in the Crime Details Form); not decided by the Court
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness accounts of P.W.3 and P.W.6, corroborated by P.Ws. 7 and 11; medical examination of P.W.3 (P.W.1, Exhibits P1A and P1B); FIR registered at 10:45 pm and contemporaneous documents (Exhibits P7, P1A, P1B, P10); post-mortem evidence of P.W.10 and recovery of weapons at the accused's instance
witness_credibility: P.W.3 (injured eyewitness) found cogent in every respect and his presence accepted; P.W.6 supported him; P.Ws. 7 and 11 corroborated; P.W.15 (investigating officer) found not untruthful; P.W.10 evidence found fully supportive; non-examination of Ranganath Sharma and minor discrepancies held not to affect the case
trial_duration: offence: 27 June 1997; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 7 September 2006; Supreme Court: 29 September 2015
legal_representation: Appellants: Tripurari Ray, Dhirendra Singh Parmar, Suresh Kumar Sharma, Rajinder Singh, Susheel Tomar, Abha R. Sharma. State: Arjun Garg, Manish Yadav, Mishra Saurabh
investigation_status: FIR registered at 10:45 pm on 27 June 1997; scene inspected 11:10 pm; medical and post-mortem requisitions made; arrests 28 June 1997; seizure 29 June 1997; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Delay in forwarding the Express Report (s.157 CrPC) to the Magistrate, received 1:20 pm on 30 June 1997; Court assumed the delay without deciding it and found no serious prejudice
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed (07.09.2006). Supreme Court: appeals dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Arrest and seizure, section 27 statements and eyewitness and medical evidence establish involvement; delay in Express Report caused no prejudice; the FIR and evidence were genuine
defence_argument: FIR was ante-dated; the injuries to P.W.3 were fake and his presence doubtful; the FIR and Crime Details Form omitted names and details; delay in Express Report; the eyewitness Ranganath Sharma was not examined; the appellants were falsely implicated
legal_principle_applied: Delay in forwarding the report to the Magistrate is not fatal unless prejudice is shown; an injured eyewitness has special status and convincing evidence is needed to discredit him; contemporaneous records and other clinching evidence outweigh minor discrepancies
precedent_relied_upon: Pala Singh v. State of Punjab (1972) 2 SCC 640; State of Karnataka v. Main Patel (1996) 8 SCC 167; Bhajan Singh @ Harbhajan Singh v. State of Haryana (2011) 7 SCC 421
